newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae group claims near victory.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae group claims near victory.

text.p: A dissident group of Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae) shareholders on Friday claimed near victory for their reorganization plan, even though the 23 million votes they have so far fall short of a majority.
"We are extremely pleased by this strong vote in support of our proposals," Albert Lord, a Sallie Mae director and leader of the group, said after a special shareholder meeting.

Lord's group, the Committee to Restore Value, said it had some 23 million votes in favor. Some 15 million holders voted against the proposal to make the government sponsored enterprise a private company able to provide student loans directly.
That leaves the votes on about 13 million shares uncast, while the group's tallying continues through May 29.
"While we are enjoying this 60/40 margin for the time being over the management slate, I think it is only appropriate to tell you this margin was a very very difficult achievement," Lord said.
The company also scheduled a meeting for its own privatization plan and slate of directors for May 15 and has challenged in court the validity of the group's special meeting today and its votes.

"It is clear that the (Committee to Restore Value) failed to get the support for their plan that they were seeking and we are looking forward to the May 15 meeting, which is the one that really counts," a Sallie Mae spokeswoman said.

Lord is confident his group will receive the majority it needs, as mandated by Congress last year when it enacted legislation requiring the agency, which has nearly $50 billion in assets, to go private or be liquidated altogether.
After the shareholder vote, Lord urged the company's chairman, William Arceneaux, to call a special board meeting to install the dissident group's slate of directors.

"I am calling on Chairman Arceneaux not only to listen, but to immediately call a board meeting of this company at which time he should withdraw his management reorganization plan before there is any further unraveling internally of this company," Lord said.
Sallie Mae purchases guaranteed loans from lenders. Under Lord's plan, the private entity would focus primarily on direct lending rather than purchasing loans.
"I see incredible opportunities in the huge vibrant growing student loan marketplace," Lord said.
Jonathan Gray, an analyst with Sanford C Bernstein & Co in New York said Lord's plan is promising.

"The notion of originating student loans is a very appealing idea because any loans that they originate rather than buy would increase the profit margin on that business by almost 70 percent," Gray said.
